tanya: quick heads-up — found an oddity in the python sampleapp where logs start with request id but later lines show '-' instead of the id after our otel/redact middleware runs. small repro below.

ev an: can you paste the log snippet + env?

tanya: sure. repro: send header X-Request-Id: zxy-999. first line shows it, subsequent lines become dash.
```
2026-09-02T14:03:12Z INFO handler incoming request req_id=zxy-999 method=POST
2026-09-02T14:03:12Z INFO runtime req_id= - model=redwood-1
2026-09-02T14:03:12Z INFO response req_id= - status=200
```

tanya: env: REDWOOD_PY_SDK=0.9.3, REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS="authorization,request-id", OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext

ev an: that looks like the redactor is matching "request-id" (canonical) and removing header before our logging context is attached. does our middleware read headers early?

tanya: middleware reads header in request middleware and sets contextvar 'request_id' immediately. but our otel hook runs in a later stage and I think deletes the original header object which some logger adapters still reference.

chia: fwiw node sample app doesn't show this — we must have a Python-specific path where we mutate request.headers in place. we used to copy headers on sanitize but last change optimized that out.

ev an: workaround: set REDWOOD_LOG_REDACT=false or change REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS to explicit x-request-id instead of request-id. Not ideal though.

tanya: yes, workaround works. Opening INF-3304.

infra-bot: INF-3304 created by tanya — "python sampleapp: redaction hook deletes propagated request id causing blanks in logs" — https://redwood.company/infra/INF-3304

chia: proposal: never mutate request.headers in place. create a sanitized dict and attach it to request.sanitized_headers. ensure logger context is populated from request contextvars and not directly from request.headers pointer. add unit and integration test that asserts request_id persists in all log lines.

ev an: also ensure REDWOOD_REDACT_HEADERS parser treats header names case-insensitively and normalizes x- prefixes. we'll match both 'request-id' and 'x-request-id' when appropriate.

tanya: adding another wrinkle — some customers have middleware that reads request.headers lazily. so even if we copy sanitized headers, if logger adapter holds a reference to original headers object, we need to avoid in-place mutations altogether.

chia: noted. I'll push a small patch: copy headers to sanitized_headers and change redact hook to operate on that. Add test that attaches a fake logger adapter which accesses headers after redaction to ensure no mutation.

ev an: thanks. once PR is up tag me and tanya. aim to ship micro patch this week.

tanya: thanks all — documented the repro in the ticket and the sampleapp README will get a short note on redaction config edge cases (x-request-id vs request-id).

infra-bot: Release task RDW-RELEASE-912 opened for INF-3304

chia: PR opened: https://redwood.company/repo/pull/4123 — includes tests and changelog entry.

ev an: reviewing now. :thumbsup:
